rationale: The assistant correctly ordered the checks (timer/manual mode, defrost setting) before pointing to the fan element, insisted on isolating at the wall switch and verifying dead before opening the back panel, and only confirmed the element diagnosis after the customer reported the blister/split with a scorch mark, matching the hidden truth. Part advice was appropriately tied to the model number from the rating plate with no universal-fit claims, and sensible engineer escalation triggers (burnt connectors, no heat after swap, lack of confidence) were given. The only minor gap is that it never directly asked the customer for the model number or the thermostat neon status, leaving the exact part unnamed, though this is acceptable given the instructions to match by model.
